concepts.title: Root, Stem and Leaf with Their Modifications

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Root, Stem and Leaf with Their Modifications' refers to.
questions.a: The flowering plant body shows a root system bearing root hairs and root caps, a stem with nodes and internodes bearing buds, and leaves with lamina; each organ shows modifications such as tap and fibrous roots, tubers, tendrils and thorns, and storage or climbing leaves.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Root, Stem and Leaf with Their Modifications'.
questions.a: Modifications like storage roots of carrot, stem tendrils of cucumber and leaf tendrils of peas reflect adaptation to storage, support and defence functions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Root, Stem and Leaf with Their Modifications' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5.2 The Root, 5.3 The Stem, 5.4 The Leaf (source: kebo105.txt sections 5.2-5.4)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Inflorescence, Flower and Its Parts' refers to.
questions.a: The flower is a modified shoot bearing four whorls of calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium arranged on thalamus, and flowers are arranged in racemose or cymose inflorescence; symmetry, merosity, aestivation and placentation describe its structure.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Inflorescence, Flower and Its Parts'.
questions.a: A flower is actinomorphic or zygomorphic, trimerous tetramerous or pentamerous, and its gynoecium may be apocarpous or syncarpous with superior or inferior ovary.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Inflorescence, Flower and Its Parts' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5.5 The Inflorescence, 5.6 The Flower (source: kebo105.txt sections 5.5-5.6)

concepts.title: Fruit, Seed Structure and Semi-technical Description

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fruit, Seed Structure and Semi-technical Description' refers to.
questions.a: After fertilisation the ovary becomes the fruit and ovules become seeds; the seed shows embryo with cotyledons, seed coat and endosperm as in maize, and plants are described in semi-technical language with floral formula and floral diagram, as seen in fabaceae, solanaceae and liliaceae.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fruit, Seed Structure and Semi-technical Description'.
questions.a: The floral formula with its symbols of bract, symmetry, merosity, fusion and ovary position condenses the family characters of fabaceae, solanaceae and liliaceae.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Fruit, Seed Structure and Semi-technical Description' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5.7 The Fruit, 5.8 The Seed, 5.9 Description of Plant Families (source: kebo105.txt sections 5.7-5.9)
